newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Lyonnaise des Eaux/Cie de Suez deal.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Lyonnaise des Eaux/Cie de Suez deal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it had cleared the merger between Lyonnaise des Eaux and Compagnie de Suez saying that it would not pose any competition problems on the quasi-totality of the markets concerned.
It said in a statement that the only concerns had arisen in the market for waste management in Belgium where the two partners would have held a "very strong position".

But Lyonnaise, a French utilities giant, had proposed selling the "major part" of its Belgian activities for the collection of domestic and industrial waste. The two partners also agreed that one or the other would divest its interests in the field of detoxication of special industrial waste in Belgium.

"The divestment proposed practically removes the effects of the operation on the three markets where the position of the parties was very strong and allows for the emergence of a viable competitor," the statement said.

The merger, which will create a global utilities heavyweight with annual sales of more than 200 billion French francs ($34.3 billion), was filed for EU regulatory approval at the end of April. ($ = 5.825 French Francs)
